patients.label: Case 1: 16-year-old woman with a giant benign left breast phyllodes tumor treated by periareolar mastopexy excision

identity_evidence.quote: A 16-year-old woman reported rapid enlargement of a large mass in her left breast over 12 months.

attribution_limitations: Breast asymmetry is stated as the patient's ("her breast asymmetry") and as the aim of the operation, but no examination sentence describes its degree or timing.

The abstract says "A biopsy was constant with a benign phyllodes tumor" while the case text names a fine-needle aspiration biopsy and a Tru-Cut needle biopsy; the abstract wording is a less specific restatement.
The surgical technique paragraph mixes general present-tense technique description with past-tense steps applied to the patient; only past-tense or caption-linked steps are recorded as performed.
Conclusion statements about favorable aesthetic results and minimal postoperative scarring describe the technique in general, not a specific patient finding.

The operative-step sentences (wide local excision, incision, deepithelialization, parenchymal fixation, round block closure) do not name the left breast; body site and laterality of these steps are left unstated.

The biopsy result is worded "consistent with" and the final diagnosis comes from histopathology of the removed tumor; the diagnosis is recorded once (confirmed, histopathology) and the biopsy results stay as observations.

claims.text: A 16-year-old woman visited an outpatient clinic with rapid enlargement of a large left breast mass over 12 months. Examination showed a huge mass occupying the lower quadrants of the left breast with expansion of the overlying skin and nipple areolar complex, and the authors describe her breast asymmetry. Ultrasonography showed a lobulated, well-circumscribed solid mass.
